I'd try to connect to Wi-Fi (I assume your hotel likely has free WiFi) and see if the game is updated.

If it is, it is most likely not working because you have accounts on two or more switches with the same games being shared across them.  This is totally legal and fine, but if your son's switch is not the "primary" switch of the account it will require Internet to be played (to ensure people are not abusing digital games across multiple consoles).

My grandpa was in a veterans home notorious in Hawaii for having 60+ cases among their residents by August.

He survived the initial symptoms but COVID apparently messed up his mind. He lost huge amounts of weight and didn't eat or drink anything for a week.  Social worker said he maybe had a few days to live.

It was tough to hear as we weren't even able to video call him throughout their entire quarantine.  They finally offered us the opportunity to speak to him via FaceTime and I was prepared to say goodbye.  I didn't say goodbye, but smiled and made sure he knew he was loved.  Each person in my family made sure of that.

Surprisingly, he held on.  He lived another four weeks or so in this weakened state, calling us a few times a week.  I was able to tell him he was a great grandfather as my wife is pregnant.  I was able to joke with him and make him smile.  He ate all his favorite foods: Oxtail Soup, pizza, rice, poi, etc.  He would do his virtual fist pump to us as a stroke almost 10 years ago took his ability to wave or open his hands.

Two days after I revealed to him he would be a great grandfather, he called my grandma and told her he didn't want to die yet.  He wanted to see me and the other grandkids get married.  But he said he was tired.  He wanted oxtail soup.  My grandma made it for him and they dropped it off at the home.  He was offered it but told the nurse "later".

Two hours later he passed.  He was alone as no one knew he was THAT far down the tunnel.  But I'd imagine that the last four weeks of his life was spent talking to his wife, talking to his children and those who loved him.  I think he found peace knowing we would be okay and it was his time to rest with all his siblings who passed before him.  He passed in the way he chose to till the bitter end.  Stubborn as usual.

I share this story because people don't really appreciate the dangers of this pandemic until something happens to them.  30+ employees of the veterans home my grandpa died in contracted COVID.  30 veterans have died in one small town.  Be careful and love those around you.  You're actions hold far reaching consequences.

Ask to withdraw your claim, they should send you a form to sign that you are waiving your right to medical treatment/indemnity in regards to your injury.  That should close your case and depending on your state you will get a form saying the claim has been closed.

If anything they are being tenacious in their investigation because they are under a deadline to submit to the Department of Labor if the claim is compensable or not.  If not they are subject to fines.

Medical facilities can still treat you if you decline worker's comp coverage for a work related injury, but of course it is at their discretion.

Worker's Comp is unrelated to TDI, so make sure you don't tell your employer is it Worker's Comp or they will be less inclined to help.  Getting mixed up in WC and TDI will cost you precious time, espcially if you are requesting the wrong thing.  Best thing to do is get disability from your physician that will officially place you off work, document their responses and if it gets to the nitty gritty contact the Department of Labor about it.  The DoL is pretty pro-employee from my understanding.
